title: How Light Bulbs Evolved
upload_title: How Light Evolved 💡 From Campfires to LEDs #shorts #engineering

beats.text: For most of history, night meant darkness.
First came fire. Warm, but smoky, and dangerous indoors.
Clay oil lamps burned olive oil or animal fat through a wick, for thousands of years.
Then candles of wax and tallow, dripping and burning down by morning.
Brighter lamps burned whale oil, and whales were hunted in huge numbers to fuel them.
In the 1800s, cities lit their streets with gas lamps, fed by pipes under the road.
In 1879, Thomas Edison made a light bulb that lasted long enough to sell.
But those bulbs turned about 90 percent of their power into heat.
Today, LEDs use a fraction of the power, and one bulb can shine for over 20 years.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
